|}
In the central area of Bizen Province, around the [[:en:Okayama Domain|Okayama Domain]] (near present-day [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Okayama|Okayama City]], [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita Ward]], and the {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}}), or from Itakuramura Mashin of the [[:en:Niwase Domain|Niwase Domain]], located near [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] (the junction of the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]), a route extends via [[:en:Hayashima|Hayashima]], {{ill|Chayamachi District|ja|茶屋町地区|lt=Chayamachi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chayamachi District|1=Chayamachi Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11617964}}, {{ill|Fujito District|ja|藤戸地区|lt=Fujito|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujito District|1=Fujito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624064}}, {{ill|Yukayama|ja|由加山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yukayama|1=Yuga Mountain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577570}}, {{ill|Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|ja|児島地域 (倉敷市)|lt=Kojima|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|1=Kojima Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388647}}, and {{ill|Shimotsui District|ja|下津井地区|lt=Shimotsui|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsui District|1=Shimotsui|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361095}}, and by ferry ({{ill|Ferry|ja|渡し船|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ferry|1=flat-bottomed ferry|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2878108}}) joins the above-mentioned Marugame Kaidō. In particular, with respect to the route originating from the Okayama Domain, it is counted among the six known as the '''Okayama Domain Six Official Routes'''<ref>“Konpira Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 30|National Route 30]], the '''main route'''); “Kamogata Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 2|National Route 2]]); “Matsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 180|National Route 180]]—overlapping with [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] along the way); “Kurashiki Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|ja|岡山県道27号岡山吉井線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 27|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472480}}); “Tsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 53|National Route 53]]); and “Ushimado Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja|岡山県道28号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道28号岡山牛窓線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 28|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472488}}).</ref> Furthermore, since this route—beyond Hayashima—passes through Yukayama, a local center of faith, it has preserved the custom of '''dual pilgrimage''', whereby pilgrims visit both {{ill|Main Yuka Shrine|ja|由加神社本宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main Yuka Shrine|1=Yuga Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577571}} and {{ill|Rendai-ji|ja|蓮台寺 (倉敷市)|lt=Rendai-ji|lt_ja=蓮台寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rendai-ji|1=Rendai-Ji (Kurashiki)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11621649}} (associated with {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}}) for protection against misfortune before proceeding to Konpira.

==== '''Meo Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|2}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=173}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=21}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=152}}
|}
Starting at an ichirizuka that once existed near the present {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}} (former Sen'ami Bridge), the route proceeds west through the Omotecho 3-chōme Shopping District, then heads south along {{ill|Yanagawa-suji|ja|柳川筋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagawa-suji|1=Yanagawa-suji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11534296}}, turns west at the {{ill|Daionji Intersection|ja|大雲寺前停留場|lt=Daionji Intersection|lt_ja=大雲寺交差点|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daionji Intersection|1=Daiunzi-mae Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11441813}}, then continues southwest via the Daiku Intersection (in front of Okayama City Hall), passes to the west of the north side of [[:en:Ōmoto Station|Ōmoto Station]], and then heads south along the tracks of the [[:en:Uno Line|Uno Line]] toward Hayashima.<ref name="k-ourai" /> It is a direct route from the center of Okayama to Yukayama and Konpira. From Hayashima (at the Matsuosaka Intersection) onward, it coincides with the route described below for the Niwase Konpira Orai.

==== '''Niwase Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|2}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=173}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=21}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=162}}
|}
This is the route via the so-called {{ill|Kamogata Orai|ja|鴨方往来|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamogata Orai|1=Kamogata Orai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675579}}, which passes through many commercial districts opened in the city, and was used by those combining business with pilgrimage. In the former territory of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] (Bizen, Bitchu, and Bingo), when referring to “Konpira Orai” the term in particular denotes this '''Niwase Konpira Orai'''. (However, it is not uncommon to refer to both this route and the later-described '''Kibitsu Konpira Orai''' collectively as “Niwase Konpira Orai”, since both routes use Niwase and Nudagawa in Kita Ward, Okayama City as their starting or relay points.) From the aforementioned ichirizuka at Omotecho (former Sen'ami Bridge) to the north side of Ōmoto Station, the path is identical to that of the Ōmoto–Meo Konpira Orai; however, on the latter route one proceeds straight west without turning at the intersection when heading south, passing through Kita-Nagase (near {{ill|Okayama Dome|ja|岡山ドーム|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Dome|1=Okayama Dome|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472050}} and [[:en:Kitanagase Station|Kita-Nagase Station]]).

==== '''Kibitsu (Ichinomiya/Mashin) Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|53}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=27}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=42}}
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|180}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=389}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=245}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=151}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=162}}
|}
This route, intended purely for regional [[:en:Pilgrimage|Pilgrimage]] and for praying for a safe journey, not only covers Konpira and Yukayama but also incorporates the various [[:en:Ichinomiya|Ichinomiya]] of Bizen and Bitchu—shrines that serve as the guardian deities of the journey. When viewed from the ichirizuka at former Sen'ami Bridge, the route ascends north in a direction diametrically opposed to the Ōmoto–Meo and Niwase Konpira Orais, following the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] all the way to {{ill|Kibitsu|ja|吉備津|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kibitsu|1=Kibitsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412649}} in Okayama City.<ref name="k-ourai" /> On the Sanyōdō, after visiting [[:en:Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsu Hikon Shrine]] in the Ichinomiya area and then entering Kibitsu—after which one crosses the [[:en:Magane Ichirizuka|Mashin Ichirizuka]] and turns south to reach [[:en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)|Kibitsu Shrine]]—the turning point is considered either the row of pine trees within the shrine grounds or, in some cases, Itakura-juku further to the west, where lanterns representing Konpira, Yukayama, and Kibitsu still remain. Just outside the torii on the southwest side of Kibitsu Shrine is a road marker directing pilgrims to Konpira, from which the true Kibitsu Konpira Orai begins. In this route the starting point of the Konpira Orai is considered to be the Sen'ami Bridge ichirizuka (the junction with the Okayama Domain Six Official Routes) when including a visit to Kibitsu Hikon Shrine, or the Mashin Ichirizuka (the junction with the former Sanyōdō) when including a visit to Kibitsu Shrine. Beyond Kibitsu Shrine, the route follows {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja|岡山県道389号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道389号吉備津松島線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 389|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472579}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja|岡山県道245号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道245号真金吉備線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 245|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472450}}, and then the municipal Kawairu Niwase Line of Okayama City southward to Niwase Orai (also known as Kamogata Orai), eventually reaching the Yanagawa marker at Nudagawa.<ref name="k-ourai" /> Many of the Konpira Orai markers in the Kibitsu area, including those near the starting point at Nudagawa, indicate both “Konpira-bound to the south/west toward Kurashiki/Tamashima” and “Kibitsu Shrine-bound to the north.” However, nowadays some consider the marker at {{ill|Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja|應徳寺の道標|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Nudagawa, Kita Ward, to be the starting point—equating it with the Niwase Konpira Orai.

From the “Nudagawa Road Marker,” where the Niwase and Kibitsu Konpira Orais converge, the route heads west through residential areas, crosses the {{ill|Ashimori River|ja|足守川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashimori River|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 笹ヶ瀬川|1=Sasagase River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602473}}, and continues south along a municipal road near Okayama Prefectural Route 153 before merging with it. It then descends southwest along the north side of the hill on which the Okayama Prefectural General Distribution Center stands, crosses [[:en:Japan National Route 2|National Route 2]] and the {{ill|Okayama Bypass|ja|岡山バイパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Bypass|1=Okayama bypass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472054}} in the Muzu area, and via Okayama Prefectural Route 185 reaches [[:en:Hayashima|Hayashima]]. At Matsuosaka Intersection it merges with the Meo Konpira Orai and joins Okayama Prefectural Route 152; at the intersection with Route 165 it turns south toward {{ill|Chayamachi District|ja|茶屋町地区|lt=Chayamachi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chayamachi District|1=Chayamachi Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11617964}} and {{ill|Fujito District|ja|藤戸地区|lt=Fujito|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujito District|1=Fujito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624064}}. From Fujito, the route continues further south, detouring broadly along the coast of the Seto Inland Sea at the foot of [[:en:Mount Washu|Washiyama]], and (in some cases, after passing a tunnel known as the '''Ouginone Tunnels''' located on the mid-slope of Washiyama beyond the Kojima urban area) descends the mountain to the port. From {{ill|Shimotsui Port|ja|下津井港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsui Port|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 下津井地区|1=Shimotsui|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361095}}, a ferry takes travelers onto the Marugame Kaidō.

== '''Tadozu Kaidō''' ==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|319}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=25}}
|}
A road from {{ill|Tadozu Port|ja|多度津港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadozu Port|1=Tadotsu Port|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11430689}} to [[:en:Zentsūji, Kagawa|Zentsūji]], Ikuno, Ōasa, and others leads to Kotohira. Like the Marugame Kaidō, it was frequently used by pilgrims arriving by Konpira ship; however, many of its users came from western Japan and Kyushu. It is said that during the [[:en:Tenpō|Tenpō era]], when the {{ill|Tadozu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadozu Domain|1=Tadozu Domain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109356835}} undertook a major renovation of Tadozu Port, this route became even busier than the Marugame Kaidō.

The road between Tadozu and Kotohira was constructed as the Shikoku New Road by the politician {{ill|Ōkubo Kennojō|ja|大久保諶之丞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkubo Kennojō|1=Ōkubo Jinnojo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11431895}} during the Meiji period. The current {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 25|ja|香川県道25号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 25|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道25号善通寺多度津線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 25|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667518}} and [[:en:Japan National Route 319|National Route 319]] follow its course, running parallel to [[:en:Shikoku Railway Company|JR Shikoku]] and the [[:en:Dosan Line|Dosan Line]].

|{{Ja_Route_Sign|438}}
|}
A road from [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]] crossing the [[:en:Sanuki Mountains|Sanuki Mountains]] to Kotohira. The name of Awa-chō within Kotohira Town derives from the large number of visitors from [[:en:Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa Province]]. Although several highways exist connecting Awa and Sanuki Provinces, the route from [[:en:Miyoshi, Tokushima|Awa Ikeda]] (displayed as “Awa Ikeda”) via {{ill|Inonohana Pass|ja|猪ノ鼻峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inonohana Pass|1=Inonohana Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11571839}}, Zaitadogawa, and the Mominoki Pass to Kotohira is known as the Awa Betsu Kaidō. This highway was later developed as part of the Shikoku New Road by {{ill|Ōkubo Kennojō|ja|大久保諶之丞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkubo Kennojō|1=Ōkubo Jinnojo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11431895}} in the Meiji period and subsequently designated as [[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]. Running parallel is the [[:en:Shikoku Railway Company|JR Shikoku]] Dosan Line.

Pilgrims from Awa, closely associated with Konpira Shrine, often combined their visit with that to {{ill|Hasakura-ji|ja|箸蔵寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasakura-ji|1=Hashikura-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603428}} (known as Konpira Oku no-in). The highway connecting Konpira Shrine and Hasakura-ji—not via Inonohana from Zaitada but via Nikenchaya—is known as the Hasakura Kaidō. Although never developed as a vehicular road, the old route has been established as a hiking trail known as {{ill|Shikoku no Michi|ja|四国のみち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikoku no Michi|1=Roads of Shikoku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11419660}}.

From [[:en:Tsurugi, Tokushima|Sadamitsu]] (displayed as “Sadamitsu”), across {{ill|Santō Pass|ja|三頭越|lt=Santō Pass|lt_ja=三頭峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Santō Pass|1=Santō Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11358314}}, then through Kubo-ya, Zōda, Shijō, and on to Kotohira, most of the Awa Kaidō was later designated as [[:en:Japan National Route 438|National Route 438]]. Although the mountain pass section was slow to be modernized for automobiles, in 1997 the {{ill|Santō Tunnel|ja|三頭トンネル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Santō Tunnel|1=Santō Tunnel|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11358310}} finally opened, easing vehicular traffic. In Mima Town, Mima City, a once-buried torii from the old highway has been revived through local residents’ efforts.<ref>[http://www.topics.or.jp/localNews/news/2011/05/2011_130628816198.html Revival of the Symbolic Torii in Mima Town] (Tokushima Shimbun, May 25, 2011)</ref>

== '''Iyo–Tosa Kaidō''' ==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|11}}
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|377}}
|}
A road from [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] along the {{ill|Suihada Coast|ja|燧灘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suihada Coast|1=Hiuchi Sea|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11569288}} to Toyohama, then inland via {{ill|Iyo Pass|ja|伊予見峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Pass|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Ushiyaguchi of Kotohira. In addition to pilgrims from [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo]], many pilgrims from [[:en:Tosa Province|Tosa]]—arriving via the [[:en:Tosa Kaidō|Tosa (North) Kaidō]]—used this route. Many of the lanterns and offerings remaining along the highway were donated by the people of Iyo and Tosa. During the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period, activists from Tosa (the [[:en:Shishi (Japan)|Samurai activists]]) also used this road, and a statue of [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] was erected at Ushiyaguchi. Additionally, a short distance away lies Hirotani Cemetery, where the graves of successive abbots of Konpira Daigongen are located. The current [[:en:Japan National Route 377|National Route 377]] follows the course of this highway.

'''Konpira Kaidō''' (金毘羅街道) refers to the pilgrimage route developed to connect various regions with [[:en:Kotohira-gū|Konpira Shrine]] (located in [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]], [[:en:Nakatado District, Kagawa|Nakatado District]], [[:en:Kotohira, Kagawa|Kotohira Town]]) and is classified as a [[:en:Kaidō|Kaidō]]. Multiple routes exist, and in some regions it is also known as '''Konpira Ōrai''' (金毘羅往来).

Among them, the Takamatsu Kaidō, Marugame Kaidō, Tadotsu Kaidō, Awa Kaidō, and Iyo/Tosa Kaidō—which were particularly well used—are collectively known as the '''Konpira Five Highways''' (金毘羅五街道). In addition to these major routes, other roads used for pilgrimages to Konpira were also referred to as either Konpira Kaidō or Konpira Ōrai. In the following sections of this article, the pilgrimage routes and highways that are historically closely associated with the "Konpira Five Highways" and the related network will be explained.
==Overview==

{{ill|Konpira Kaido|ja|金毘羅街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Kaido|qq=}} is a pilgrimage route of {{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Japan|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It connects many Konpira Shrines<ref>{{Cite web|title=Arched Stone Bridge {{!|qq=draft}} FACILITIES {{!}} GUIDE |url=http://www.shikokumura.or.jp/en/guide/facilities/arched-stone-bridge/ |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=SHIKOKUMURA |language=ja}}</ref> on [[Shikoku]]<ref>https://www.skr.mlit.go.jp/kikaku/88-kei/en/scenery/50_ehime.html</ref>. It is a [[:en:Kaidō|Kaidō]].

{{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]]s dedicated to [[Ōmononushi]]. Due to [[Shinbutsu-shūgō]] they often also worship [[Konpira Gongen]]

They are part of the famous Inahachikonten Shrines (稲八金天神社)  of the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy]] alongside [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari shrine]], [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]], {{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, and [[Tenmangū|Tenmangu Shrine]].

== Overview ==
[[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], as the faith in [[:en:Konpira Gongen|Konpira Daigongen]]—the guardian deity of maritime traffic—spread among the common people, pilgrimages to Konpira became popular, and many devotees began visiting from all over the country. On the pilgrimage routes used by numerous travelers, lanterns and boundary stones were erected, and the roads were developed as highways.

From the mid‐Meiji period onward, as {{ill|Railway|ja|鉄道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Railway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=railway|WD=Q22667}}s and [[:en:Car|Automobile]]s emerged, the Konpira Kaidō as a pedestrian route declined, and new roads following the course of the old highway were built. Today many of these roads have been designated as prefectural or national routes. Meanwhile, the roads formerly known as the “Konpira Kaidō” became classified as {{ill|Old Road|ja|旧道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Old Road|1=Old Road|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11511138}}, and many lost their original appearance through regional road improvements, residential land development, and {{ill|Land Readjustment|ja|区画整理|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Land Readjustment|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 土地区画整理事業|1=land readjustment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423116}}.

In some areas once traversed by highways and traffic routes, remnants of the old road markers can still be seen. However, many of these markers were relocated during regional land development, and in such cases the actual orientation may not match that indicated by the marker—caution is advised. Moreover, many of these markers bear the inscription “sugu konpira,” which is to be interpreted as “directly to Konpira” (i.e. “proceed straight ahead toward Konpira”) rather than indicating physical proximity.

== '''Takamatsu Kaidō''' (高松街道) (also known as '''Kotohira Kaidō''' (琴平街道))
==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|32}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=282}}
|}
It is also known as Kotohira Kaidō, Takamatsu Konpira Kaidō, among other names. Connecting Takamatsu Castle with various parts of Sanuki Province, the [[:en:Takamatsu Domain|Takamatsu Domain]]’s '''Sanuki Five Highways'''<ref>“Kotohira Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]—the Takamatsu Mannō section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|ja|香川県道266号勅使室新線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 266|lt_ja=香川県道266号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 266|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667524}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|ja|香川県道282号高松琴平線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 282|lt_ja=香川県道282号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 282|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667533}} known as the '''main route'''); “Marugame Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]]—the Takamatsu–Marugame section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 175 Kigake Gōhigashi Line|ja|香川県道175号衣掛郷東線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 175|lt_ja=香川県道175号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 175 Kigake Gōhigashi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 175|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667466}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 33 Takamatsu-Zentōji Line|ja|香川県道33号高松善通寺線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|lt_ja=香川県道33号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 33 Takamatsu-Zentōji Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 33|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667538}}); “Shido Kaidō” (prototype of the route linking the Takamatsu–Hakutori section of [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]]—predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 155 Mure New Line|ja|香川県道155号牟礼中新線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 155|lt_ja=香川県道155号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 155 Mure New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 155|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667450}}, and connecting from Hakutori via the predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 1 Tokushima Hikida Line|ja|徳島県道・香川県道1号徳島引田線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 1|lt_ja=香川県道1号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 1 Tokushima Hikida Line|1=Tokushima Prefectural Road and Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 1|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11490196}} known as the “Awa Kaidō” linking Takamatsu and Tokushima domains); “{{ill|Nagao Kaidō|ja|長尾街道 (香川県)|lt=Nagao Kaidō|lt_ja=長尾街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagao Kaidō|1=Nagao Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q60985920}}” (predecessor of {{ill|Sanuki Higashi Kaidō|ja|さぬき東街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanuki Higashi Kaidō|1=Sanuki Higashi Highway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11268197}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 10 Takamatsu-Nagao Ōuchi Line|ja|香川県道10号高松長尾大内線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 10|lt_ja=香川県道10号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 10 Takamatsu-Nagao Ōuchi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 10|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667418}}); and “Busshōzan Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 193|National Route 193]]—the Takamatsu–Shioe section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 166 Iwasaki-Takamatsu Line|ja|香川県道166号岩崎高松線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 166|lt_ja=香川県道166号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 166 Iwasaki-Takamatsu Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 166|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667458}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 280 Takamatsu-Kagawa Line|ja|香川県道280号高松香川線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 280|lt_ja=香川県道280号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 280 Takamatsu-Kagawa Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 280|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667531}}, connecting the “Shioe Kaidō” from Shioe Onsen) among the five highways.<ref>Refer to the brochure “Konpira Kaidō” (published by the Konpira Pilgrimage Guide Council).</ref> Its starting point is [[:en:Takamatsu Castle (Sanuki)|Takamatsu Castle]] (Tamamo Castle); the outer moat was spanned by {{ill|Tokiwabashi (Takamatsu)|ja|常盤橋 (高松市)|lt=Tokiwabashi|lt_ja=常盤橋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokiwabashi (Takamatsu)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, located near the present {{ill|Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|ja|高松三越|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|1=Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11670275}}. From Kuririn, the route passes through such places as Enza, Hatada Jūsanzuka, Takimiya, Okada, and Enkei in the interior of Kagawa before reaching Kotohira. Because the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松平氏|1=Matsudaira clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1141077}} of the Takamatsu Domain strongly protected Konpira Shrine, the highway was developed early on; the {{ill|Demba-sho|ja|伝馬|lt=Demba-sho|lt_ja=伝馬所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Demba-sho|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 駅伝制|1=post-horses|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11381453}} was located at Kurikuma, while the starting-point [[:en:Ichirizuka|Ichirizuka]] on the Takamatsu side was placed at Kamimachi, Enza, Fukuiya, Tō, Ono, Okada, and Shijō—and the towns along the highway flourished as [[:en:Shukuba|Post town]]s.

The modern Takamatsu Kaidō comprises the current {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|ja|香川県道266号勅使室新線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 266|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667524}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|ja|香川県道282号高松琴平線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 282|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667533}} (the former National Route 32) and its bypass ([[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]), with portions overlapping the old highway. Between Enza and Kotohira, the [[:en:Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railway]] and its [[:en:Kotoden Kotohira Line|Kotohira Line]] run almost parallel.

In the Chūzan region, the primary river [[:en:Doki River|Doki River]] is known as Haraikawa in the midstream area where the Takamatsu Kaidō crosses it—said to be so because pilgrims on their way to Konpira Shrine purified themselves in this river.

== '''Marugame Kaidō''' (丸亀街道) (Konpira Orai, 金毘羅往来)
==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=4|align=left}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=204|align=left}} 
|}
Starting from {{ill|Marugame Port|ja|丸亀港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Marugame Port|1=Port of Marugame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11368011}}, this route proceeds via Nakabu, Gunke, Yokita, and others to Kotohira. Because the overland distance was short and the terrain flat, many pilgrims—arriving by {{ill|Konpira Ship|ja|金毘羅船|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Ship|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from places such as {{ill|Osaka|ja|大坂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大阪|1=Ōsaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11439906}} or from [[:en:Bizen Province|Bizen Province]]—used it. It is said that during the [[:en:Enkyō (Edo period)|Enkyō era]] a regular ship service operated between Osaka and Marugame, making it the busiest of the many Konpira Kaidō routes. Today, roads following its course include {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|ja|香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|lt_ja=香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}} and {{ill|Kagawa/Tokushima Prefectural Route 4 Marugame-Miyoshi Line|ja|香川県道・徳島県道4号丸亀三好線|lt=Prefectural Route 4|lt_ja=香川県道4号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa/Tokushima Prefectural Route 4 Marugame-Miyoshi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road and Tokushima Prefectural Road Route 4|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667559}}.

At {{ill|Marugame Port|ja|丸亀港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Marugame Port|1=Port of Marugame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11368011}}, from the Taisuke lantern or from the {{ill|Sanuki Hamakaidō|ja|さぬき浜街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanuki Hamakaidō|1=Sanuki Hamakaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11268199}} ({{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 193 Kawazu-Marugame Line|ja|香川県道193号川津丸亀線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 193|lt_ja=香川県道193号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 193 Kawazu-Marugame Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 193|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667484}}) beneath the Kyogoku Ohashi—where {{ill|Kyogoku Funatama Shrine|ja|京極船魂神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyogoku Funatama Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} is located—head south along a municipal road toward [[:en:Marugame Station|Marugame Station]]. Pass under the elevated structure of the [[:en:Yosan Line|Yosan Line]], and at Tsūchō turn west. In front of Marugame Station, after crossing {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|ja|香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|lt_ja=香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}}, immediately enter the museum street of Hamamachi (a narrow lane located about 50 m west of the intersection—with the south side of the {{ill|Inokuma Genichirō Contemporary Art Museum|ja|猪熊弦一郎現代美術館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuma Genichirō Contemporary Art Museum|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 丸亀市猪熊弦一郎現代美術館|1=Marugame Genichiro-Inokuma Museum of Contemporary Art|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11367991}}) and proceed south through Nanjō Town to Nakabu Town. In Nakabu (at the marker of “Torinomeken”), turn west; however, the road descends to the southwest, passing through Nakabu’s large torii gate and continuing south. Then cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 205|ja|香川県道205号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 205|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and at the three‐way intersection of Nakabu’s three houses (marked by the Heisei-era five‐stone marker) turn east; next, cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|ja|香川県道33号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道33号高松善通寺線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 33|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667538}} and enter Yamakita Town. From the Castle West Community Center in Yamakita, turn south onto {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|ja|香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}} and enter Katsubaru Town; after passing in front of the Marugame Castle South Post Office, at a fork marked by the Heisei-era twenty-stone marker, turn west—leaving Prefectural Route 204 onto a municipal road along the town boundary—and proceed south. Cross [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]], pass along the eastern edge of Tamura Pond (a local reservoir, {{ill|Reservoir|ja|溜め池|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reservoir|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ため池|1=irrigation reservoir|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q112083751}}), and continue further south; then, passing under the Takamatsu Expressway overpass where a lantern is visible on the west side of the road, proceed south toward Gunke Town. In Sanjō Town, merge with {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 4|ja|香川県道4号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 4|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道・徳島県道4号丸亀三好線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road and Tokushima Prefectural Road Route 4|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667559}} and enter Yokita Town in [[:en:Zentsūji, Kagawa|Zentsūji City]]. Thereafter, continuing almost along Route 4, from Yokita Town pass through [[:en:Mannō, Kagawa|Mannou Town]] (Kōmon and Mannou Town Nishitakashino) and at Naeda in [[:en:Kotohira, Kagawa|Kotohira Town]], turn west. After passing through the precinct alley of {{ill|Wakamiya Shrine|ja|若宮神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakamiya Shrine|qq=}}, continue west, cross the intersection of [[:en:Japan National Route 319|National Route 319]] and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 206|ja|県道206号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 206|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} at Naeda, and proceed further west. After passing under the Dosan Line overpass, continue south along the Dosan Line. Then, without entering any alley between the [[:en:Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railway]] ([[:en:Kotoden Kotohira Line|Kotohira Line]]) and the Dosan Line, cross the Yokose level crossing; if you continue straight south, you will reach the '''High Lantern''' situated in the park “Kita Shin'en” on the east side of {{ill|Kotoden Kotohira Station|ja|琴電琴平駅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoden Kotohira Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Kotoden-Kotohira Station|WD=Q11573814}}, marking the end of the main highway.<ref>Refer to the brochure “Konpira Kaidō” (published by the Konpira Pilgrimage Guide Council).</ref> From the High Lantern, if you cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 207|ja|県道207号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 207|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and proceed straight south along Kotohira’s urban lanes, then at the intersection with the shopping arcade turn west (a right turn) and continue, you will enter the approach to Konpira Shrine.

In the central area of Bizen Province, around the [[:en:Okayama Domain|Okayama Domain]] (near present-day [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Okayama|Okayama City]], [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita Ward]], and the {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}}), or from Itakuramura Mashin of the [[:en:Niwase Domain|Niwase Domain]], located near [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] (the junction of the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]), a route extends via [[:en:Hayashima|Hayashima]], {{ill|Chayamachi District|ja|茶屋町地区|lt=Chayamachi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chayamachi District|1=Chayamachi Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11617964}}, {{ill|Fujito District|ja|藤戸地区|lt=Fujito|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujito District|1=Fujito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624064}}, {{ill|Yukayama|ja|由加山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yukayama|1=Yuga Mountain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577570}}, {{ill|Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|ja|児島地域 (倉敷市)|lt=Kojima|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|1=Kojima Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388647}}, and {{ill|Shimotsui District|ja|下津井地区|lt=Shimotsui|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsui District|1=Shimotsui|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361095}}, and by ferry ({{ill|Ferry|ja|渡し船|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ferry|1=flat-bottomed ferry|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2878108}}) joins the above-mentioned Marugame Kaidō. In particular, with respect to the route originating from the Okayama Domain, it is counted among the six known as the '''Okayama Domain Six Official Routes'''<ref>“Konpira Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 30|National Route 30]], the '''main route'''); “Kamogata Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 2|National Route 2]]); “Matsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 180|National Route 180]]—overlapping with [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] along the way); “Kurashiki Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|ja|岡山県道27号岡山吉井線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 27|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472480}}); “Tsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 53|National Route 53]]); and “Ushimado Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja|岡山県道28号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道28号岡山牛窓線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 28|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472488}}).</ref> Furthermore, since this route—beyond Hayashima—passes through Yukayama, a local center of faith, it has preserved the custom of '''dual pilgrimage''', whereby pilgrims visit both {{ill|Main Yuka Shrine|ja|由加神社本宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main Yuka Shrine|1=Yuga Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577571}} and {{ill|Rendai-ji|ja|蓮台寺 (倉敷市)|lt=Rendai-ji|lt_ja=蓮台寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rendai-ji|1=Rendai-Ji (Kurashiki)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11621649}} (associated with {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}}) for protection against misfortune before proceeding to Konpira.

Starting at an ichirizuka that once existed near the present {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}} (former Sen'ami Bridge), the route proceeds west through the Omotecho 3-chōme Shopping District, then heads south along {{ill|Yanagawa-suji|ja|柳川筋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagawa-suji|1=Yanagawa-suji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11534296}}, turns west at the {{ill|Daionji Intersection|ja|大雲寺前停留場|lt=Daionji Intersection|lt_ja=大雲寺交差点|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daionji Intersection|1=Daiunzi-mae Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11441813}}, then continues southwest via the Daiku Intersection (in front of Okayama City Hall), passes to the west of the north side of [[:en:Ōmoto Station|Ōmoto Station]], and then heads south along the tracks of the [[:en:Uno Line|Uno Line]] toward Hayashima.<ref name="k-ourai" /> It is a direct route from the center of Okayama to Yukayama and Konpira. From Hayashima (at the Matsuosaka Intersection) onward, it coincides with the route described below for the Niwase Konpira Orai.

==== '''Niwase Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|2}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=173}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=21}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=162}}
|}
This is the route via the so-called {{ill|Kamogata Orai|ja|鴨方往来|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamogata Orai|1=Kamogata Orai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675579}}, which passes through many commercial districts opened in the city, and was used by those combining business with pilgrimage. In the former territory of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] (Bizen, Bitchu, and Bingo), when referring to “Konpira Orai” the term in particular denotes this '''Niwase Konpira Orai'''. (However, it is not uncommon to refer to both this route and the later-described '''Kibitsu Konpira Orai''' collectively as “Niwase Konpira Orai”, since both routes use Niwase and Nudagawa in Kita Ward, Okayama City as their starting or relay points.) From the aforementioned ichirizuka at Omotecho (former Sen'ami Bridge) to the north side of Ōmoto Station, the path is identical to that of the Ōmoto–Meo Konpira Orai; however, on the latter route one proceeds straight west without turning at the intersection when heading south, passing through Kita-Nagase (near {{ill|Okayama Dome|ja|岡山ドーム|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Dome|1=Okayama Dome|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472050}} and [[:en:Kitanagase Station|Kita-Nagase Station]]).

This route, intended purely for regional [[:en:Pilgrimage|Pilgrimage]] and for praying for a safe journey, not only covers Konpira and Yukayama but also incorporates the various [[:en:Ichinomiya|Ichinomiya]] of Bizen and Bitchu—shrines that serve as the guardian deities of the journey. When viewed from the ichirizuka at former Sen'ami Bridge, the route ascends north in a direction diametrically opposed to the Ōmoto–Meo and Niwase Konpira Orais, following the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] all the way to {{ill|Kibitsu|ja|吉備津|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kibitsu|1=Kibitsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412649}} in Okayama City.<ref name="k-ourai" /> On the Sanyōdō, after visiting [[:en:Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsu Hikon Shrine]] in the Ichinomiya area and then entering Kibitsu—after which one crosses the [[:en:Magane Ichirizuka|Mashin Ichirizuka]] and turns south to reach [[:en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)|Kibitsu Shrine]]—the turning point is considered either the row of pine trees within the shrine grounds or, in some cases, Itakura-juku further to the west, where lanterns representing Konpira, Yukayama, and Kibitsu still remain. Just outside the torii on the southwest side of Kibitsu Shrine is a road marker directing pilgrims to Konpira, from which the true Kibitsu Konpira Orai begins. In this route the starting point of the Konpira Orai is considered to be the Sen'ami Bridge ichirizuka (the junction with the Okayama Domain Six Official Routes) when including a visit to Kibitsu Hikon Shrine, or the Mashin Ichirizuka (the junction with the former Sanyōdō) when including a visit to Kibitsu Shrine. Beyond Kibitsu Shrine, the route follows {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja|岡山県道389号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道389号吉備津松島線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 389|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472579}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja|岡山県道245号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道245号真金吉備線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 245|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472450}}, and then the municipal Kawairu Niwase Line of Okayama City southward to Niwase Orai (also known as Kamogata Orai), eventually reaching the Yanagawa marker at Nudagawa.<ref name="k-ourai" /> Many of the Konpira Orai markers in the Kibitsu area, including those near the starting point at Nudagawa, indicate both “Konpira-bound to the south/west toward Kurashiki/Tamashima” and “Kibitsu Shrine-bound to the north.” However, nowadays some consider the marker at {{ill|Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja|應徳寺の道標|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Nudagawa, Kita Ward, to be the starting point—equating it with the Niwase Konpira Orai.

From the “Nudagawa Road Marker,” where the Niwase and Kibitsu Konpira Orais converge, the route heads west through residential areas, crosses the {{ill|Ashimori River|ja|足守川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashimori River|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 笹ヶ瀬川|1=Sasagase River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602473}}, and continues south along a municipal road near Okayama Prefectural Route 153 before merging with it. It then descends southwest along the north side of the hill on which the Okayama Prefectural General Distribution Center stands, crosses [[:en:Japan National Route 2|National Route 2]] and the {{ill|Okayama Bypass|ja|岡山バイパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Bypass|1=Okayama bypass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472054}} in the Muzu area, and via Okayama Prefectural Route 185 reaches [[:en:Hayashima|Hayashima]]. At Matsuosaka Intersection it merges with the Meo Konpira Orai and joins Okayama Prefectural Route 152; at the intersection with Route 165 it turns south toward {{ill|Chayamachi District|ja|茶屋町地区|lt=Chayamachi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chayamachi District|1=Chayamachi Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11617964}} and {{ill|Fujito District|ja|藤戸地区|lt=Fujito|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujito District|1=Fujito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624064}}. From Fujito, the route continues further south, detouring broadly along the coast of the Seto Inland Sea at the foot of [[:en:Mount Washu|Washiyama]], and (in some cases, after passing a tunnel known as the '''Ouginone Tunnels''' located on the mid-slope of Washiyama beyond the Kojima urban area) descends the mountain to the port. From {{ill|Shimotsui Port|ja|下津井港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsui Port|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 下津井地区|1=Shimotsui|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361095}}, a ferry takes travelers onto the Marugame Kaidō.

== '''Tadozu Kaidō''' ==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|319}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=25}}
|}
A road from {{ill|Tadozu Port|ja|多度津港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadozu Port|1=Tadotsu Port|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11430689}} to [[:en:Zentsūji, Kagawa|Zentsūji]], Ikuno, Ōasa, and others leads to Kotohira. Like the Marugame Kaidō, it was frequently used by pilgrims arriving by Konpira ship; however, many of its users came from western Japan and Kyushu. It is said that during the [[:en:Tenpō|Tenpō era]], when the {{ill|Tadozu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadozu Domain|1=Tadozu Domain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109356835}} undertook a major renovation of Tadozu Port, this route became even busier than the Marugame Kaidō.

The road between Tadozu and Kotohira was constructed as the Shikoku New Road by the politician {{ill|Ōkubo Kennojō|ja|大久保諶之丞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkubo Kennojō|1=Ōkubo Jinnojo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11431895}} during the Meiji period. The current {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 25|ja|香川県道25号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 25|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道25号善通寺多度津線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 25|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667518}} and [[:en:Japan National Route 319|National Route 319]] follow its course, running parallel to [[:en:Shikoku Railway Company|JR Shikoku]] and the [[:en:Dosan Line|Dosan Line]].

== '''Awa Kaidō''' ==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|32}}
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|438}}
|}
A road from [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]] crossing the [[:en:Sanuki Mountains|Sanuki Mountains]] to Kotohira. The name of Awa-chō within Kotohira Town derives from the large number of visitors from [[:en:Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa Province]]. Although several highways exist connecting Awa and Sanuki Provinces, the route from [[:en:Miyoshi, Tokushima|Awa Ikeda]] (displayed as “Awa Ikeda”) via {{ill|Inonohana Pass|ja|猪ノ鼻峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inonohana Pass|1=Inonohana Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11571839}}, Zaitadogawa, and the Mominoki Pass to Kotohira is known as the Awa Betsu Kaidō. This highway was later developed as part of the Shikoku New Road by {{ill|Ōkubo Kennojō|ja|大久保諶之丞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkubo Kennojō|1=Ōkubo Jinnojo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11431895}} in the Meiji period and subsequently designated as [[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]. Running parallel is the [[:en:Shikoku Railway Company|JR Shikoku]] Dosan Line.

Pilgrims from Awa, closely associated with Konpira Shrine, often combined their visit with that to {{ill|Hasakura-ji|ja|箸蔵寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasakura-ji|1=Hashikura-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603428}} (known as Konpira Oku no-in). The highway connecting Konpira Shrine and Hasakura-ji—not via Inonohana from Zaitada but via Nikenchaya—is known as the Hasakura Kaidō. Although never developed as a vehicular road, the old route has been established as a hiking trail known as {{ill|Shikoku no Michi|ja|四国のみち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikoku no Michi|1=Roads of Shikoku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11419660}}.

From [[:en:Tsurugi, Tokushima|Sadamitsu]] (displayed as “Sadamitsu”), across {{ill|Santō Pass|ja|三頭越|lt=Santō Pass|lt_ja=三頭峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Santō Pass|1=Santō Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11358314}}, then through Kubo-ya, Zōda, Shijō, and on to Kotohira, most of the Awa Kaidō was later designated as [[:en:Japan National Route 438|National Route 438]]. Although the mountain pass section was slow to be modernized for automobiles, in 1997 the {{ill|Santō Tunnel|ja|三頭トンネル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Santō Tunnel|1=Santō Tunnel|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11358310}} finally opened, easing vehicular traffic. In Mima Town, Mima City, a once-buried torii from the old highway has been revived through local residents’ efforts.<ref>[http://www.topics.or.jp/localNews/news/2011/05/2011_130628816198.html Revival of the Symbolic Torii in Mima Town] (Tokushima Shimbun, May 25, 2011)</ref>

== '''Iyo–Tosa Kaidō''' ==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|11}}
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|377}}
|}
A road from [[:en:Ehime Prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]] along the {{ill|Suihada Coast|ja|燧灘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suihada Coast|1=Hiuchi Sea|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11569288}} to Toyohama, then inland via {{ill|Iyo Pass|ja|伊予見峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Pass|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Ushiyaguchi of Kotohira. In addition to pilgrims from [[:en:Iyo Province|Iyo]], many pilgrims from [[:en:Tosa Province|Tosa]]—arriving via the [[:en:Tosa Kaidō|Tosa (North) Kaidō]]—used this route. Many of the lanterns and offerings remaining along the highway were donated by the people of Iyo and Tosa. During the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period, activists from Tosa (the [[:en:Shishi (Japan)|Samurai activists]]) also used this road, and a statue of [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] was erected at Ushiyaguchi. Additionally, a short distance away lies Hirotani Cemetery, where the graves of successive abbots of Konpira Daigongen are located. The current [[:en:Japan National Route 377|National Route 377]] follows the course of this highway.

[[File:Kagawa_Pref_R282_祓川橋西.jpg|thumb|Torii on Takamatsu Kaidō (Mannou Town's {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|ja|香川県道282号高松琴平線|lt=Kagawa Prefecture Route 282|lt_ja=香川県道282号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefecture Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 282|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667533}})]]
'''Konpira Kaidō''' (金毘羅街道) refers to the pilgrimage route developed to connect various regions with [[:en:Kotohira-gū|Konpira Shrine]] (located in [[:en:Kagawa Prefecture|Kagawa Prefecture]], [[:en:Nakatado District, Kagawa|Nakatado District]], [[:en:Kotohira, Kagawa|Kotohira Town]]) and is classified as a [[:en:Kaidō|Kaidō]]. Multiple routes exist, and in some regions it is also known as '''Konpira Ōrai''' (金毘羅往来).

Among them, the Takamatsu Kaidō, Marugame Kaidō, Tadotsu Kaidō, Awa Kaidō, and Iyo/Tosa Kaidō—which were particularly well used—are collectively known as the '''Konpira Five Highways''' (金毘羅五街道). In addition to these major routes, other roads used for pilgrimages to Konpira were also referred to as either Konpira Kaidō or Konpira Ōrai. In the following sections of this article, the pilgrimage routes and highways that are historically closely associated with the "Konpira Five Highways" and the related network will be explained.
==Overview==

{{ill|Konpira Kaido|ja|金毘羅街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Kaido|qq=}} is a pilgrimage route of {{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Japan|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It connects many Konpira Shrines<ref>{{Cite web|title=Arched Stone Bridge {{!|qq=draft}} FACILITIES {{!}} GUIDE |url=http://www.shikokumura.or.jp/en/guide/facilities/arched-stone-bridge/ |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=SHIKOKUMURA |language=ja}}</ref> on [[Shikoku]]<ref>https://www.skr.mlit.go.jp/kikaku/88-kei/en/scenery/50_ehime.html</ref>. It is a [[:en:Kaidō|Kaidō]].

{{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]]s dedicated to [[Ōmononushi]]. Due to [[Shinbutsu-shūgō]] they often also worship [[Konpira Gongen]]

They are part of the famous Inahachikonten Shrines (稲八金天神社)  of the [[Shrine Consolidation Policy]] alongside [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari shrine]], [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]], {{ill|Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrines|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, and [[Tenmangū|Tenmangu Shrine]].

== Overview ==
[[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], as the faith in [[:en:Konpira Gongen|Konpira Daigongen]]—the guardian deity of maritime traffic—spread among the common people, pilgrimages to Konpira became popular, and many devotees began visiting from all over the country. On the pilgrimage routes used by numerous travelers, lanterns and boundary stones were erected, and the roads were developed as highways.

From the mid‐Meiji period onward, as {{ill|Railway|ja|鉄道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Railway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=railway|WD=Q22667}}s and [[:en:Car|Automobile]]s emerged, the Konpira Kaidō as a pedestrian route declined, and new roads following the course of the old highway were built. Today many of these roads have been designated as prefectural or national routes. Meanwhile, the roads formerly known as the “Konpira Kaidō” became classified as {{ill|Old Road|ja|旧道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Old Road|1=Old Road|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11511138}}, and many lost their original appearance through regional road improvements, residential land development, and {{ill|Land Readjustment|ja|区画整理|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Land Readjustment|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 土地区画整理事業|1=land readjustment|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423116}}.

In some areas once traversed by highways and traffic routes, remnants of the old road markers can still be seen. However, many of these markers were relocated during regional land development, and in such cases the actual orientation may not match that indicated by the marker—caution is advised. Moreover, many of these markers bear the inscription “sugu konpira,” which is to be interpreted as “directly to Konpira” (i.e. “proceed straight ahead toward Konpira”) rather than indicating physical proximity.

== '''Takamatsu Kaidō''' (高松街道) (also known as '''Kotohira Kaidō''' (琴平街道))
==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|32}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=282}}
|}
It is also known as Kotohira Kaidō, Takamatsu Konpira Kaidō, among other names. Connecting Takamatsu Castle with various parts of Sanuki Province, the [[:en:Takamatsu Domain|Takamatsu Domain]]’s '''Sanuki Five Highways'''<ref>“Kotohira Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]—the Takamatsu Mannō section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|ja|香川県道266号勅使室新線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 266|lt_ja=香川県道266号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 266|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667524}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|ja|香川県道282号高松琴平線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 282|lt_ja=香川県道282号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 282|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667533}} known as the '''main route'''); “Marugame Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]]—the Takamatsu–Marugame section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 175 Kigake Gōhigashi Line|ja|香川県道175号衣掛郷東線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 175|lt_ja=香川県道175号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 175 Kigake Gōhigashi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 175|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667466}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 33 Takamatsu-Zentōji Line|ja|香川県道33号高松善通寺線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|lt_ja=香川県道33号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 33 Takamatsu-Zentōji Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 33|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667538}}); “Shido Kaidō” (prototype of the route linking the Takamatsu–Hakutori section of [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]]—predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 155 Mure New Line|ja|香川県道155号牟礼中新線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 155|lt_ja=香川県道155号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 155 Mure New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 155|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667450}}, and connecting from Hakutori via the predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 1 Tokushima Hikida Line|ja|徳島県道・香川県道1号徳島引田線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 1|lt_ja=香川県道1号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 1 Tokushima Hikida Line|1=Tokushima Prefectural Road and Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 1|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11490196}} known as the “Awa Kaidō” linking Takamatsu and Tokushima domains); “{{ill|Nagao Kaidō|ja|長尾街道 (香川県)|lt=Nagao Kaidō|lt_ja=長尾街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagao Kaidō|1=Nagao Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q60985920}}” (predecessor of {{ill|Sanuki Higashi Kaidō|ja|さぬき東街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanuki Higashi Kaidō|1=Sanuki Higashi Highway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11268197}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 10 Takamatsu-Nagao Ōuchi Line|ja|香川県道10号高松長尾大内線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 10|lt_ja=香川県道10号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 10 Takamatsu-Nagao Ōuchi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 10|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667418}}); and “Busshōzan Kaidō” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 193|National Route 193]]—the Takamatsu–Shioe section, predecessor of {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 166 Iwasaki-Takamatsu Line|ja|香川県道166号岩崎高松線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 166|lt_ja=香川県道166号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 166 Iwasaki-Takamatsu Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 166|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667458}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 280 Takamatsu-Kagawa Line|ja|香川県道280号高松香川線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 280|lt_ja=香川県道280号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 280 Takamatsu-Kagawa Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 280|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667531}}, connecting the “Shioe Kaidō” from Shioe Onsen) among the five highways.<ref>Refer to the brochure “Konpira Kaidō” (published by the Konpira Pilgrimage Guide Council).</ref> Its starting point is [[:en:Takamatsu Castle (Sanuki)|Takamatsu Castle]] (Tamamo Castle); the outer moat was spanned by {{ill|Tokiwabashi (Takamatsu)|ja|常盤橋 (高松市)|lt=Tokiwabashi|lt_ja=常盤橋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokiwabashi (Takamatsu)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, located near the present {{ill|Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|ja|高松三越|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|1=Takamatsu Mitsukoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11670275}}. From Kuririn, the route passes through such places as Enza, Hatada Jūsanzuka, Takimiya, Okada, and Enkei in the interior of Kagawa before reaching Kotohira. Because the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 松平氏|1=Matsudaira clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1141077}} of the Takamatsu Domain strongly protected Konpira Shrine, the highway was developed early on; the {{ill|Demba-sho|ja|伝馬|lt=Demba-sho|lt_ja=伝馬所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Demba-sho|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 駅伝制|1=post-horses|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11381453}} was located at Kurikuma, while the starting-point [[:en:Ichirizuka|Ichirizuka]] on the Takamatsu side was placed at Kamimachi, Enza, Fukuiya, Tō, Ono, Okada, and Shijō—and the towns along the highway flourished as [[:en:Shukuba|Post town]]s.

The modern Takamatsu Kaidō comprises the current {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|ja|香川県道266号勅使室新線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 266 Chokushishitsu New Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 266|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667524}} and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|ja|香川県道282号高松琴平線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 282 Takamatsu-Kotohira Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 282|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667533}} (the former National Route 32) and its bypass ([[:en:Japan National Route 32|National Route 32]]), with portions overlapping the old highway. Between Enza and Kotohira, the [[:en:Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railway]] and its [[:en:Kotoden Kotohira Line|Kotohira Line]] run almost parallel.

In the Chūzan region, the primary river [[:en:Doki River|Doki River]] is known as Haraikawa in the midstream area where the Takamatsu Kaidō crosses it—said to be so because pilgrims on their way to Konpira Shrine purified themselves in this river.

== '''Marugame Kaidō''' (丸亀街道) (Konpira Orai, 金毘羅往来)
==
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=4|align=left}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Kagawa|number=204|align=left}} 
|}
Starting from {{ill|Marugame Port|ja|丸亀港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Marugame Port|1=Port of Marugame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11368011}}, this route proceeds via Nakabu, Gunke, Yokita, and others to Kotohira. Because the overland distance was short and the terrain flat, many pilgrims—arriving by {{ill|Konpira Ship|ja|金毘羅船|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Ship|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from places such as {{ill|Osaka|ja|大坂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大阪|1=Ōsaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11439906}} or from [[:en:Bizen Province|Bizen Province]]—used it. It is said that during the [[:en:Enkyō (Edo period)|Enkyō era]] a regular ship service operated between Osaka and Marugame, making it the busiest of the many Konpira Kaidō routes. Today, roads following its course include {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|ja|香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|lt_ja=香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}} and {{ill|Kagawa/Tokushima Prefectural Route 4 Marugame-Miyoshi Line|ja|香川県道・徳島県道4号丸亀三好線|lt=Prefectural Route 4|lt_ja=香川県道4号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa/Tokushima Prefectural Route 4 Marugame-Miyoshi Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road and Tokushima Prefectural Road Route 4|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667559}}.

At {{ill|Marugame Port|ja|丸亀港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Marugame Port|1=Port of Marugame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11368011}}, from the Taisuke lantern or from the {{ill|Sanuki Hamakaidō|ja|さぬき浜街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanuki Hamakaidō|1=Sanuki Hamakaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11268199}} ({{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 193 Kawazu-Marugame Line|ja|香川県道193号川津丸亀線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 193|lt_ja=香川県道193号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 193 Kawazu-Marugame Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 193|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667484}}) beneath the Kyogoku Ohashi—where {{ill|Kyogoku Funatama Shrine|ja|京極船魂神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyogoku Funatama Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} is located—head south along a municipal road toward [[:en:Marugame Station|Marugame Station]]. Pass under the elevated structure of the [[:en:Yosan Line|Yosan Line]], and at Tsūchō turn west. In front of Marugame Station, after crossing {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|ja|香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|lt=Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|lt_ja=香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204 Marugame Station Line|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}}, immediately enter the museum street of Hamamachi (a narrow lane located about 50 m west of the intersection—with the south side of the {{ill|Inokuma Genichirō Contemporary Art Museum|ja|猪熊弦一郎現代美術館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inokuma Genichirō Contemporary Art Museum|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 丸亀市猪熊弦一郎現代美術館|1=Marugame Genichiro-Inokuma Museum of Contemporary Art|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11367991}}) and proceed south through Nanjō Town to Nakabu Town. In Nakabu (at the marker of “Torinomeken”), turn west; however, the road descends to the southwest, passing through Nakabu’s large torii gate and continuing south. Then cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 205|ja|香川県道205号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 205|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and at the three‐way intersection of Nakabu’s three houses (marked by the Heisei-era five‐stone marker) turn east; next, cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|ja|香川県道33号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 33|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道33号高松善通寺線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 33|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667538}} and enter Yamakita Town. From the Castle West Community Center in Yamakita, turn south onto {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|ja|香川県道204号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 204|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道204号丸亀停車場線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road Route 204|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667491}} and enter Katsubaru Town; after passing in front of the Marugame Castle South Post Office, at a fork marked by the Heisei-era twenty-stone marker, turn west—leaving Prefectural Route 204 onto a municipal road along the town boundary—and proceed south. Cross [[:en:Japan National Route 11|National Route 11]], pass along the eastern edge of Tamura Pond (a local reservoir, {{ill|Reservoir|ja|溜め池|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reservoir|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ため池|1=irrigation reservoir|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q112083751}}), and continue further south; then, passing under the Takamatsu Expressway overpass where a lantern is visible on the west side of the road, proceed south toward Gunke Town. In Sanjō Town, merge with {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 4|ja|香川県道4号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 4|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香川県道・徳島県道4号丸亀三好線|1=Kagawa Prefectural Road and Tokushima Prefectural Road Route 4|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11667559}} and enter Yokita Town in [[:en:Zentsūji, Kagawa|Zentsūji City]]. Thereafter, continuing almost along Route 4, from Yokita Town pass through [[:en:Mannō, Kagawa|Mannou Town]] (Kōmon and Mannou Town Nishitakashino) and at Naeda in [[:en:Kotohira, Kagawa|Kotohira Town]], turn west. After passing through the precinct alley of {{ill|Wakamiya Shrine|ja|若宮神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakamiya Shrine|qq=}}, continue west, cross the intersection of [[:en:Japan National Route 319|National Route 319]] and {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 206|ja|県道206号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 206|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} at Naeda, and proceed further west. After passing under the Dosan Line overpass, continue south along the Dosan Line. Then, without entering any alley between the [[:en:Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railway]] ([[:en:Kotoden Kotohira Line|Kotohira Line]]) and the Dosan Line, cross the Yokose level crossing; if you continue straight south, you will reach the '''High Lantern''' situated in the park “Kita Shin'en” on the east side of {{ill|Kotoden Kotohira Station|ja|琴電琴平駅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoden Kotohira Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Kotoden-Kotohira Station|WD=Q11573814}}, marking the end of the main highway.<ref>Refer to the brochure “Konpira Kaidō” (published by the Konpira Pilgrimage Guide Council).</ref> From the High Lantern, if you cross {{ill|Kagawa Prefectural Route 207|ja|県道207号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagawa Prefectural Route 207|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and proceed straight south along Kotohira’s urban lanes, then at the intersection with the shopping arcade turn west (a right turn) and continue, you will enter the approach to Konpira Shrine.

=== Konpira Orai ===
[[File:Konpira orai sign.jpg|thumb|200px|Sign of Konpira Orai (Hayashima Town)]]

|}
In the central area of Bizen Province, around the [[:en:Okayama Domain|Okayama Domain]] (near present-day [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Okayama|Okayama City]], [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita Ward]], and the {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}}), or from Itakuramura Mashin of the [[:en:Niwase Domain|Niwase Domain]], located near [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] (the junction of the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]]), a route extends via [[:en:Hayashima|Hayashima]], {{ill|Chayamachi District|ja|茶屋町地区|lt=Chayamachi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chayamachi District|1=Chayamachi Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11617964}}, {{ill|Fujito District|ja|藤戸地区|lt=Fujito|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujito District|1=Fujito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624064}}, {{ill|Yukayama|ja|由加山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yukayama|1=Yuga Mountain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577570}}, {{ill|Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|ja|児島地域 (倉敷市)|lt=Kojima|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojima Area (Kurashiki)|1=Kojima Area|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388647}}, and {{ill|Shimotsui District|ja|下津井地区|lt=Shimotsui|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsui District|1=Shimotsui|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361095}}, and by ferry ({{ill|Ferry|ja|渡し船|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ferry|1=flat-bottomed ferry|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2878108}}) joins the above-mentioned Marugame Kaidō. In particular, with respect to the route originating from the Okayama Domain, it is counted among the six known as the '''Okayama Domain Six Official Routes'''<ref>“Konpira Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 30|National Route 30]], the '''main route'''); “Kamogata Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 2|National Route 2]]); “Matsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 180|National Route 180]]—overlapping with [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] along the way); “Kurashiki Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|ja|岡山県道27号岡山吉井線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 27 Okayama-Yoshii Line|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 27|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472480}}); “Tsuyama Orai” (prototype of [[:en:Japan National Route 53|National Route 53]]); and “Ushimado Orai” (prototype of {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja|岡山県道28号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 28|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道28号岡山牛窓線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 28|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472488}}).</ref> Furthermore, since this route—beyond Hayashima—passes through Yukayama, a local center of faith, it has preserved the custom of '''dual pilgrimage''', whereby pilgrims visit both {{ill|Main Yuka Shrine|ja|由加神社本宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main Yuka Shrine|1=Yuga Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577571}} and {{ill|Rendai-ji|ja|蓮台寺 (倉敷市)|lt=Rendai-ji|lt_ja=蓮台寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rendai-ji|1=Rendai-Ji (Kurashiki)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11621649}} (associated with {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Daigongen|qq=}}) for protection against misfortune before proceeding to Konpira.

==== '''Meo Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|2}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=173}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=21}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=152}}
|}
Starting at an ichirizuka that once existed near the present {{ill|Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|ja|岡山表町商店街|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Omotecho Shopping Street|1=Omotechō Shōtengai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472751}} (former Sen'ami Bridge), the route proceeds west through the Omotecho 3-chōme Shopping District, then heads south along {{ill|Yanagawa-suji|ja|柳川筋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yanagawa-suji|1=Yanagawa-suji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11534296}}, turns west at the {{ill|Daionji Intersection|ja|大雲寺前停留場|lt=Daionji Intersection|lt_ja=大雲寺交差点|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daionji Intersection|1=Daiunzi-mae Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11441813}}, then continues southwest via the Daiku Intersection (in front of Okayama City Hall), passes to the west of the north side of [[:en:Ōmoto Station|Ōmoto Station]], and then heads south along the tracks of the [[:en:Uno Line|Uno Line]] toward Hayashima.<ref name="k-ourai" /> It is a direct route from the center of Okayama to Yukayama and Konpira. From Hayashima (at the Matsuosaka Intersection) onward, it coincides with the route described below for the Niwase Konpira Orai.

==== '''Niwase Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|2}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=173}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=21}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=162}}
|}
This is the route via the so-called {{ill|Kamogata Orai|ja|鴨方往来|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamogata Orai|1=Kamogata Orai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675579}}, which passes through many commercial districts opened in the city, and was used by those combining business with pilgrimage. In the former territory of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] (Bizen, Bitchu, and Bingo), when referring to “Konpira Orai” the term in particular denotes this '''Niwase Konpira Orai'''. (However, it is not uncommon to refer to both this route and the later-described '''Kibitsu Konpira Orai''' collectively as “Niwase Konpira Orai”, since both routes use Niwase and Nudagawa in Kita Ward, Okayama City as their starting or relay points.) From the aforementioned ichirizuka at Omotecho (former Sen'ami Bridge) to the north side of Ōmoto Station, the path is identical to that of the Ōmoto–Meo Konpira Orai; however, on the latter route one proceeds straight west without turning at the intersection when heading south, passing through Kita-Nagase (near {{ill|Okayama Dome|ja|岡山ドーム|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Dome|1=Okayama Dome|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472050}} and [[:en:Kitanagase Station|Kita-Nagase Station]]).

==== '''Kibitsu (Ichinomiya/Mashin) Konpira Orai''' ====
{| 
|-
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|53}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=27}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=42}}
|{{Ja_Route_Sign|180}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=389}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=245}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=151}}
|{{Ja_Pref_Route_Sign|pref=Okayama|number=162}}
|}
This route, intended purely for regional [[:en:Pilgrimage|Pilgrimage]] and for praying for a safe journey, not only covers Konpira and Yukayama but also incorporates the various [[:en:Ichinomiya|Ichinomiya]] of Bizen and Bitchu—shrines that serve as the guardian deities of the journey. When viewed from the ichirizuka at former Sen'ami Bridge, the route ascends north in a direction diametrically opposed to the Ōmoto–Meo and Niwase Konpira Orais, following the former [[:en:San'yōdō|Sanyōdō]] all the way to {{ill|Kibitsu|ja|吉備津|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kibitsu|1=Kibitsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412649}} in Okayama City.<ref name="k-ourai" /> On the Sanyōdō, after visiting [[:en:Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsu Hikon Shrine]] in the Ichinomiya area and then entering Kibitsu—after which one crosses the [[:en:Magane Ichirizuka|Mashin Ichirizuka]] and turns south to reach [[:en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)|Kibitsu Shrine]]—the turning point is considered either the row of pine trees within the shrine grounds or, in some cases, Itakura-juku further to the west, where lanterns representing Konpira, Yukayama, and Kibitsu still remain. Just outside the torii on the southwest side of Kibitsu Shrine is a road marker directing pilgrims to Konpira, from which the true Kibitsu Konpira Orai begins. In this route the starting point of the Konpira Orai is considered to be the Sen'ami Bridge ichirizuka (the junction with the Okayama Domain Six Official Routes) when including a visit to Kibitsu Hikon Shrine, or the Mashin Ichirizuka (the junction with the former Sanyōdō) when including a visit to Kibitsu Shrine. Beyond Kibitsu Shrine, the route follows {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja|岡山県道389号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 389|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道389号吉備津松島線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 389|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472579}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja|岡山県道245号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okayama Prefectural Route 245|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 岡山県道245号真金吉備線|1=Okayama Prefectural Road Route 245|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11472450}}, and then the municipal Kawairu Niwase Line of Okayama City southward to Niwase Orai (also known as Kamogata Orai), eventually reaching the Yanagawa marker at Nudagawa.<ref name="k-ourai" /> Many of the Konpira Orai markers in the Kibitsu area, including those near the starting point at Nudagawa, indicate both “Konpira-bound to the south/west toward Kurashiki/Tamashima” and “Kibitsu Shrine-bound to the north.” However, nowadays some consider the marker at {{ill|Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja|應徳寺の道標|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtoku-ji Road Marker|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Nudagawa, Kita Ward, to be the starting point—equating it with the Niwase Konpira Orai.
